route: self-describing item codes (ONE* pair abbreviations) diffed against the OSF questionnaire PDFs + route 9 (response-frequency/recode matching against the deposit's own scored columns) + aggregate test-retest correlation for the TWO* block
evidence: OSF deposit 'Pictorial Materialism Test_database_clean.sav' holds the 64 raw columns under exactly the IRW item codes; non-missing cells across those 64 columns = 7392, equal to the live table's 7392 rows, at 204 per ONE* column (paper N=204) and 27 per TWO* column (paper retest n=27). Route 9 against the deposit's own recoded columns: predicting the study's rONE*/rTWO* (1 = chose the materialistic picture) as (raw == position of the material picture in the code's own pair label) reproduces 32/32 ONE* columns and 32/32 TWO* columns exactly, cell for cell including the NA pattern. The check is not vacuous - 16 codes name the material picture first and 16 name it second - so it fixes resp 1 = first-named picture (A on the page) and resp 2 = second-named (B). The ONE* block is additionally pinned item by item: each code carries a two-token Polish pair abbreviation, and the 32 sentences in the girls'/boys' questionnaire PDFs name those same two pictures in that same order, 32/32; the shipped option_text carries the code-named picture at the right resp level 128/128. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the 32 TWO* codes carry no pair abbreviation, so nothing distinguishes them item by item. Their pairing to ONE* rests on the shared numeric suffix (1,3,4,...,40), on the 32/32 recode agreement (one bit each, which separates material-first from material-second but not the 16 codes within either class), and on an aggregate signal - the materialistic-choice rate per item correlates r=0.743 between ONE_k and TWO_k over 32 pairs against 2000 random re-pairings (mean -0.002, 97.5th pct 0.353, p<0.0005). Per-item test-retest agreement is too weak at n=27 to break it: 0.624 on-diagonal vs 0.529 off-diagonal, and the diagonal is the strict maximum for only 3 of 32 items. So two TWO* items in the same direction class could in principle be swapped without any number here changing. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

Route 5 (subscale block structure) + route 1 (published per-item means), both run against the hypothesis that this deposit's ct_N is item N of the 40-item TRWCAS/EACTDR pool. n=235, 23 items, 19 with a published factor assignment. Mean within-factor r = 0.211 (org 0.289, cond 0.186, socio 0.158) vs mean between-factor r = 0.216 -- i.e. no block structure; 5/17 items load strongest on their hypothesised subscale, at or below chance. Synonym pairs that must cohere do not: ct_6 x ct_32 (autonomy over content vs over methods) r=0.066; ct_33 x ct_36 (noisy vs uncomfortable workspace) r=0.183; ct_15 x ct_27 r=0.138. Unrelated pairs top the matrix: ct_31 x ct_32 r=0.782, ct_27 x ct_31 r=0.751, ct_1 x ct_2 r=0.684, ct_23 x ct_29 r=0.557. Per-item means rank-correlate rho=0.204 with the developers' own basic-education sample (UVA technical report Tabelas 15.4-15.6) across the 19 shared items, with all five hypothesised socio-professional items +1.10 to +2.20 higher (ct_29 3.86 vs 1.66, ct_15 4.03 vs 2.04, ct_27 3.03 vs 1.62, ct_32 2.73 vs 1.63, ct_6 1.64 vs 1.60). NO_ROUTE, not PARTIAL: these routes do not pin any item -- they only DISCONFIRM the one candidate mapping, so nothing about ct_N is established. No __items.csv was written and no item text shipped; this row records that the mapping was checked and failed, not that a shipped table was verified. What this does NOT establish: what ct_N actually means -- that needs Psicologia em Pesquisa e44013, which is HTTP 401 from here.
